name: Escape Vector
tagline: Public-domain spaceflight pushed to hard black and white, with one re-entry red for everything alive.
summary: A self-funded builder who left orbit on purpose. The hero is a landing site: a crater field built from twenty CSS 3D contour slices, where a red probe reads altitude under the cursor and locks onto real product beacons standing on the high ground. NASA photography, Trouvelot engravings and Haeckel's radiolarians make it feel like a real archive, and decode-into-place type and spring physics make it feel engineered.
voice: Precise, a little defiant, never corporate. Short declaratives with physics in them. Example: "Four up. Seven came down."
motion: Everything has mass: hand-rolled damped springs for tilt, lift and float, and text that arrives as noise and locks in left to right.
sound: Off until asked; then tiny sine blips on probe locks, decoded figures and new downlink events, pitched down like telemetry.
mark: A vector capital A whose tip has come loose and floats, tilted 10 degrees in burn red; the tip launches on hover.
